_meta.rule: Logistics change often. Every fact has a source; anything marked confidence 'verify' came from secondary sources or sources disagreed. The app always tells users to confirm with the official body before paying or booking.

format.model: 3 Core sections (FAR, AUD, REG) + 1 Discipline you choose (BAR, ISC or TCP)
format.testing: Continuous testing year-round at Prometric centres (book about 45 days ahead)
format.structure: 5 testlets per section: 2 MCQ testlets, then 3 TBS testlets. A standard 15-minute break is offered after testlet 3.

creditWindow.text: Most jurisdictions now give a rolling 30-month window to pass all remaining sections after the first pass (NASBA Model Rule 5-7, amended 2023). A few still use 18 months, and some use 36. The start date (score release vs exam date) also varies.

international.text: The CPA Exam can be taken in India at Prometric centres. You must first be found eligible by a U.S. jurisdiction that participates in international administration, receive a Notice to Schedule (NTS), pay the international testing fee, wait 24 hours and then book with Prometric.
international.notParticipatingNote: These boards don't take part in INTERNATIONAL testing. A candidate using them must sit the exam inside the U.S. This is about the test location, not nationality.
international.intlFeeNote: The international testing fee is charged PER SECTION on top of normal exam fees. Sources disagree on the 2026 amount ($460–$510), so check NASBA before paying.

jurisdictionAdvice.headline: No U.S. state bans Indian citizens. What differs is the education rules, whether a Social Security Number (SSN) or U.S. residency is required at exam or licence stage, and whether the board allows international testing.
choose: Get a NASBA International Evaluation Services (NIES) evaluation of your degree and CA/CMA credits. Ask it to recommend jurisdictions.

Pick a board that (a) participates in international testing, (b) accepts your credit mix, and (c) issues a LICENCE without an SSN or U.S. residency, if you want the licence and not just the exam pass.
Check whether that board offers the 120-credit + 2-year-experience pathway if you don't have 150 credits.

commonlyUsed.note: Often chosen by India-based candidates. Reported to accept an affidavit instead of an SSN.
Often chosen. Reports conflict on whether an SSN is needed for licensure.
Reported to need 150 credits to sit the exam (most boards need 120). Has a 36-month credit window.
Often listed as SSN-free. Some practitioners warn not all Indian coursework is counted. New 120-credit pathway from 1 Jan 2026.
Listed by some guides as not requiring an SSN for the exam. Has a 120-credit + 1,800-hour experience pathway.

pathways: Traditional: 150 semester credits + typically 1 year of verified experience + exam.
New pathway (adopted by many states from 2025–27): bachelor's in accounting (120 credits) + 2 years of experience + exam. Effective dates vary by state, e.g. Alaska 2026, California 2027.
licensure.ethics: Most boards require an ethics exam after passing, often the AICPA Professional Ethics exam (PETH). Some states have their own.

lifecycle.title: Check eligibility
lifecycle.detail: Collect transcripts (degree + CA/CMA) and get a NIES credential evaluation.

lifecycle.title: Choose your state board
lifecycle.detail: Use the Location Advisor. Confirm international testing, credit acceptance and the licence SSN rule.

lifecycle.title: Apply & pay exam fees
lifecycle.detail: Apply through the board or CPA Central. Pay the application fee and section fees.

lifecycle.title: Receive Notice to Schedule (NTS)
lifecycle.detail: Note the NTS expiry date. You must test before it.

lifecycle.title: Register for international testing
lifecycle.detail: Testing outside the U.S.? Pay NASBA's international fee per section, then wait 24 hours.

lifecycle.title: Book Prometric seat
lifecycle.detail: Book about 45 days ahead. Choose your city and date.

lifecycle.title: Study & sit section 1
lifecycle.detail: Most people start with FAR or the section they find hardest.

lifecycle.title: Pass all 4 sections within credit window
lifecycle.detail: Usually 30 months from your first pass. Track the deadline in the app.

lifecycle.title: Pass ethics exam
lifecycle.detail: As your board requires, often AICPA PETH.

lifecycle.title: Verify experience
lifecycle.detail: 1 year (150-credit route) or 2 years (120-credit route), signed by a licensed CPA.

lifecycle.title: Apply for CPA licence
lifecycle.detail: Submit to your board. Check SSN or residency requirements.

lifecycle.title: Join AICPA & keep CPE current
lifecycle.detail: Membership is optional. Continuing education (CPE) is required to keep the licence.

format.notes: Computer-based at Prometric. MCQ only, with no negative marking. Part II is graded only if Part I is passed. Pass marks are not published (results are reported as quartiles).

fees.text: Exam fee about USD 600 (early) or USD 800 (standard) per part, plus a one-time programme enrolment fee on first registration. Deadlines are 11:59 pm U.S. Eastern Time.

india.text: Prometric centres in major Indian cities. Select your centre while scheduling, before the scheduling deadline.

certification.text: Pass Part II by 31 December of the 4th year after passing Part I. Submit 2 years of full-time relevant work experience within 10 years of passing Part II (extended from 5 years, effective May 2025). Experience can be before or after the exams. Internships and part-time work don't count.

lifecycle.title: Create GARP account & enrol
lifecycle.detail: Pay the one-time enrolment fee with your first Part I registration.

lifecycle.title: Register for Part I (early window saves money)
lifecycle.detail: Watch the early-registration deadline in the app's calendar.

lifecycle.title: Schedule Prometric seat
lifecycle.detail: Pick an Indian city and date before the scheduling deadline.

lifecycle.title: Pass Part I
lifecycle.detail: 100 questions, 4 hours.

lifecycle.title: Pass Part II by 31 Dec of year 4 after Part I
lifecycle.detail: 80 questions, 4 hours. Can be taken in the same window as Part I, but is graded only if Part I is passed.

lifecycle.title: Submit 2 years' work experience
lifecycle.detail: Within 10 years of passing Part II. Full-time risk-related work only.

lifecycle.title: Receive FRM certification
lifecycle.detail: GARP reviews your experience and awards the certificate.

lifecycle.title: GARP membership & CPD
lifecycle.detail: Keep membership and complete continuing professional development (CPD) as GARP requires.
